html:
A preacher and scholar from Najd in central Arabia whose movement, known to outsiders as Wahhabism, became the official creed of the Saudi states.

Born to a family of judges, he studied in Medina and Basra. He taught a strict idea of God's oneness and attacked practices common at the time, such as visiting saints' tombs and asking them for help, which he called a form of idolatry. He drew on the Hanbali school of law and on the writings of Ibn Taymiyya.

In 1744 he made a pact with Muhammad bin Saud, ruler of the small town of Diriyah. The preacher gave religious backing; the emir gave protection and spread the teaching by conquest. This alliance built the Emirate of Diriyah, the first Saudi state, which by the early 1800s held most of Arabia, including Mecca, until Ottoman Egyptian armies destroyed it in 1818.

The pact between the two families lasted. When Ibn Saud founded modern Saudi Arabia, the descendants of Ibn Abd al-Wahhab, the Al ash-Sheikh, led its religious establishment.
sum: A preacher and scholar from Najd in central Arabia whose movement, known to outsiders as Wahhabism, became the official creed of the Saudi states.
